title: Digest: Same senses, different minds in Heliconius butterflies
content:
Abstract
What neural changes underlie the evolution of novel behavior? Does behavioral innovation require enhanced sensory input, or can it arise through reorganization of existing neural circuits? Hodge et al. (2026) show that the enlarged mushroom bodies associated with specialized foraging in Heliconius butterflies reflect localized circuit restructuring, while peripheral sensory pathways remain largely conserved. These findings suggest that cognitive innovation can emerge through changes in integrative brain centers without expansion of sensory systems.
